evidence_status: Local, reproducible implementation evidence for pre-existing temporary-entry attacks; not a publisher signature, zero-knowledge proof, post-creation race defense or crash-durability proof.

criteria.evidence: save_atomic now allocates every candidate with OpenOptions write plus create_new. Existing entries produce AlreadyExists and are skipped; other I/O errors return immediately. Oversize serialization no longer removes a never-created predictable path.

Old symlink and hard-link processes exit 0, overwrite the sentinel victim with v4 ledger bytes and leave state sharing the victim identity. New processes exit 0 through another candidate, preserve sentinel and pre-existing link, and leave a regular state with a distinct identity.
The new regular-collision process preserves the first candidate as sentinel at its original name and exits 0; its state SHA-256 equals the no-collision new control.

With 128 pre-existing entries the new binary exits 2 with cannot allocate unique temporary state file and after 128 attempts. No state is created and all 128 sentinel files remain present and byte-identical.

verify-atomic-write-python.py derives temporary paths from recorded child PIDs, recomputes every recorded after-state from the live filesystem, passes four filesystem known answers and rejects five synthetic fake-report classes before accepting the real five-case report.
The old and new no-collision controls both exit 0 with byte-identical v4 snapshots and no temporary remainder. Wave, execution, replay, output-path and smoke anchors all pass without drift.

The implementation commit archive has no .git and was built with an initially absent CARGO_TARGET_DIR. build-all exited 0 with 106 Rust tests; its clean binary generated the final five-case differential and the independent verifier passed.

differential_summary.old: exit=0; victim becomes v4 ledger and state becomes a symlink to victim
differential_summary.new: exit=0; victim and first symlink remain sentinel/unchanged; regular independent state

differential_summary.old: exit=0; victim becomes v4 ledger and state shares its identity
differential_summary.new: exit=0; victim and first hardlink remain sentinel/shared; regular independent state

differential_summary.old: exit=0; first predictable temporary is overwritten and renamed
differential_summary.new: exit=0; first regular file remains sentinel at its original name; state equals control

differential_summary.old: exit=0; first of 128 entries is overwritten and renamed
differential_summary.new: exit=2; no state; all 128 sentinel entries preserved; explicit bounded diagnostic
exit=0; byte-identical v4 state and no temporary remainder

development_corrections.record: The first pre-exec fixture mistakenly called Python Path.with_extension and raised AttributeError before executing the target. It was corrected to with_suffix; the baseline process then ran and confirmed the overwrite. The failed fixture was not counted as a security result.

A state-lock sidecar collision was inspected but not promoted to the breakthrough: report fs::write changes sidecar contents without replacing its inode, so the stronger predictable ledger-temporary symlink chain was selected and tested instead.

not_proven: Create-new allocation closes pre-existing temporary-entry attacks, not an adversary who can replace the temporary pathname after successful creation and before rename.
No fsync, crash-power-loss durability, WAL, hostile-OS confinement, non-cooperating-writer isolation or distributed transaction semantics are added.

The atomic-write implementation commit is not covered by the earlier push and external CI receipt for 2a40df0; no cisvr ACK, KEY-SYNC-01, federation activation, QF-OS/QIOS canonical compatibility, zero-knowledge proof or distributed exactly-once claim follows.
